slot.brief: Definite integral of a rational/trigonometric function where a substitution (t = tan x or x → 1/x) or symmetry simplifies it dramatically.

verdicts.working: Let t=tan x. Then I=∫₀∞ (1+t²)/(t⁴+3t²+1) dt. Set u=t−1/t, so du=(1+t²)dt/t² and t⁴+3t²+1=t²(u²+5). Thus I=∫₋∞∞ du/(u²+5)=π/√5.

working:
$t=\tan x:\quad I=\displaystyle\int_0^\infty\dfrac{1+t^2}{t^4+3t^2+1}\,dt$.
Let $J=\displaystyle\int_0^\infty\dfrac{dt}{t^4+3t^2+1}$. The substitution $t\mapsto1/t$ gives $\displaystyle\int_0^\infty\dfrac{t^2\,dt}{t^4+3t^2+1}=J$, so $I=2J$.
With $u=t-1/t$, $du=\dfrac{1+t^2}{t^2}dt$ and $t^4+3t^2+1=t^2(u^2+5)$.
$I=\displaystyle\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}\dfrac{du}{u^2+5}=\dfrac{\pi}{\sqrt{5}}$.

Independent check: Let t=tan x. Then I=∫₀∞ (1+t²)/(t⁴+3t²+1) dt. Set u=t−1/t, so du=(1+t²)dt/t² and t⁴+3t²+1=t²(u²+5). Thus I=∫₋∞∞ du/(u²+5)=π/√5.
solution:
Let $t=\tan x$; then $I=\displaystyle\int_0^\infty\frac{1+t^2}{t^4+3t^2+1}\,dt$. Set $u=t-\frac1t$, so $du=\frac{1+t^2}{t^2}\,dt$ and $t^4+3t^2+1=t^2(u^2+5)$. Thus
$$I=\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}\frac{du}{u^2+5}=\frac{\pi}{\sqrt5}.$$
